messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: bounds + rows/columns syntax decision
parts:
So the question is, do we add named bounds
or just go with what we have now?

Now w. named bounds / named rows & cols

int a; int a;

real b; real b;

int[0,] c; int<lb=0> c;

int[0,1] d; int<lb=0,ub=1> d;

int e[10]; int e[10];

real f[4,5]; real f[4,5];

real[-1,1] g[10]; real<lb=-1,ub=1> g[10];

matrix[4,5] h; matrix[4,5] h; / matrix<rows=4,cols=5> h;

matrix[4,5] i[6]; matrix[4,5] i[6]; / matrix<rows=4,cols=5> i[6];

vector[5] j[7,8]; vector[5] j[7,8]; / vector<rows=5> j[7,8];

row_vector[9] k[10]; row_vector[9] k[10]; / row_vector<cols=9> k[10];

This leaves open doing this in the future for constrained
matrices, etc. using what we have now:

matrix<real[-1,1]>[4,5] m;

or with named constraints:

matrix<lb=-1,ub=1>[4,5] m;

and also with named rows and cols:

matrix<lb=-1,ub=1,rows=4,cols=5> m;

-------------------------

The only issue I see with what we have now is the
potential misinterpretation of similar arguments,
as in

matrix[2,3] m;
real[2,3] x;

which declares m to be a 2 x 3 matrix and x to be
a real value constrained between 2 and 3. With named bounds,
the two declarations would be

matrix[2,3] m;
real<lb=2,ub=3> x;

With named rows/cols, they would be

matrix<rows=2,cols=3> m;
real<lb=2,ub=3> x;

I'm rather leaning toward named bounds but not named rows/cols.
I think the rows/cols things is confusing, especially for
vectors vs. row vectors:

vector<rows=3> v;
row_vector<cols=3> rv;

vs. what we have w/o names:

vector[3] v;
row_vector[3] rv;

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] bounds + rows/columns syntax decision
parts:
I prefer named bounds but not named rows and columns. Thus, for example:

int[bounds=0,] c
int[bounds=0,1] d
real[bounds=-1,1] f[4,5]
matrix[bounds=-1,1][4,5] m

Another reason I don't like the "rows" and "columns" thing is what happened to R: different functions use "row", "rows", "nrow", "nrows", "col.means", "colnames", etc (and I'm probably getting some of these wrong). Sometimes column is "column" (parallel to the word "row") and sometimes it's "col" (parallel to the three-letter word "row"). Yuck! If we never use the words "row" or "column" at all, I'll be happy.

As a non-C-user, I'd go with square brackets everywhere so that users don't have to try to remember when they need angle brackets. But if you think that's silly, we can go with the angle brackets!
